overview.description: Read, wrangle, and analyse biological sequence data: FASTA/FASTQ formats, quality scores, alignment (BLAST/Bowtie), and scripting with Biopython/pandas. Nearly every wet-lab result now flows through a command line before it means anything.
objectives: work with sequence formats (FASTA, FASTQ, SAM/BAM, VCF)
read Phred quality scores and trim/QC reads
align sequences and interpret BLAST results
script analyses with Biopython / pandas and the command line

steps.description: Read, wrangle, and analyse biological sequence data: FASTA/FASTQ formats, quality scores, alignment (BLAST/Bowtie), and scripting with Biopython/pandas. Nearly every wet-lab result now flows through a command line before it means anything.
steps.intro: Bioinformatics is data literacy for biology - the ability to take raw files off an instrument and turn them into an answer, reproducibly.

instructions.title: Know your formats
instructions.description: Recognise FASTA (sequence) vs FASTQ (sequence + per-base Phred quality) and downstream SAM/BAM/VCF.

instructions.title: QC first
instructions.description: Assess read quality (FastQC), trim adapters/low-quality bases before any analysis.

instructions.title: Align & interpret
instructions.description: Map reads or BLAST a query; understand e-value, identity, and coverage before trusting a hit.

instructions.title: Script it
instructions.description: Automate parsing and summary with Biopython/pandas so the analysis is reproducible, not click-by-click.

submission.description: Take a raw FASTQ, QC and trim it, align or BLAST it, and produce a short reproducible summary - explaining each quality decision.

kits.name: Rosalind problems (free)
kits.note: Learn sequence analysis by solving real problems in the browser.

kits.name: Biopython + public data (free)
kits.note: Script FASTQ QC, alignment and parsing on a laptop; no wet lab.
